# 2026-06-09

- Long day. Locked in the Ridgeline trucks for Glen's auto parts run.
- Walked the loop after supper, about two and a half miles. Knees felt it but the back was alright.
- Brand handled a rate con on his own today without me hovering. Proud of him. See [[Brand at the company]].
- Thinking on the [[Software upgrade decision]] again. Leaning RoutePoint.

# 2026-06-08

- Wayne sent the draft P&L. Numbers look steady, thank the Lord.
- Took my statin and the aspirin like always. Need to do better on the sweet tea.
- Donna worked late at the clinic. Saved her a plate.
- Some worries running in my head tonight, wrote them down in [[Worries]] so I can sleep.

# 2026-06-07

- Church this morning. Pastor Harlan preached on contentment. Needed to hear it.
- Smoked a couple racks of ribs in the afternoon. Cody ate his weight in them.
- Quiet evening on the patio with Donna. Good day.

# 2026-06-06

- Pete from Smoky Mountain wrote about Q3 rates. Set a call for Tuesday.
- Softball got rained out so I worked in the garden instead. Tomatoes coming in.
- Keith is smoking a shoulder for our mentorship planning. Looking forward to it.
- Logged tonight's brisket prep in [[Brisket log]].

# Cholesterol and the statin

LDL was still a touch high at the spring check. Dr Pershing kept me on atorvastatin 20mg daily. Baby aspirin and the multivitamin too.

He was plain about it. Said the numbers are headed the right way but the weight is the lever I control. About twenty pounds is the difference.

## What I am trying
- Black coffee, cut back the sweet tea
- Walk most evenings, two to three miles
- Go easier on the brisket fat, save it for special

Next cholesterol check is the quarterly. Want to walk in with a better number. See [[Walking and weight]].

# Walking and weight

Keeping honest with myself here. Fifty years old, carrying more than I should.

Evenings I can get out, I walk the neighborhood loop. Two and a half miles, maybe three. Slow and steady, not breaking any records.

Saturdays there is over-40 softball at Lakeshore Park. That is about all the sprinting these old legs want.

The back stiffens up if I sit at the desk too long. Stretch in the morning, that helps. Goal is not to be an athlete, just to be around for the grandkids someday.

# Dr Pershing visit notes - May

Saw Dr Glenn Pershing at Knoxville Medical Group for the quarterly.

- Blood pressure fine
- Cholesterol still slightly elevated, stay the course on the statin
- He asked about the back. Told him it is just stiffness, nothing shooting down the leg
- Sleep is good, 10:30 to 6

He said keep walking, lose a little, come back in three months. Dentist cleaning is due at Knoxville Family Dental too, need to call.

# Sunday reflections

Pastor Harlan preached on contentment this morning at Ridgeview. Hit me where I live.

I spend a lot of weeks chasing the next load, the next client, fretting over the software and the money. The Lord has given me a good wife, healthy kids, work that puts food on the table.

Wrote it here so I remember it Tuesday when the phone is ringing off the hook. Be grateful. The business is a blessing, not a burden.

# Prayer list

- Mama June's knees, and that she keeps getting around up in Harlan
- Megan, that she stays grounded down in Nashville with all that pre-law pressure
- Cody, a good and safe football season
- Brand, finding his footing at the company
- Wisdom on the business decisions
- Thanks for Donna, every day

# Kids

## Brand (22)
Working with me now as junior associate. Sharp, a little impatient like I was. Want to teach him the trade without crushing him. See [[Brand at the company]].

## Megan (19)
Pre-law sophomore at Ridge Valley in Nashville. Calls on Sundays mostly. Worried she works too hard. Proud as can be of her.

## Cody (15)
Farragut High, varsity football. Eats like a horse, good kid. Homecoming game is in October, would not miss it.

Three good kids. Donna and I did alright.

# Donna

Forty-seven and still puts up with me after all these years. Office manager over at Valley View Family Medical.

She carries a lot, between the clinic and keeping this house running. I do not tell her enough how much I lean on her.

Took her to Northshore Brasserie for her birthday. Need to plan more of those, not just the big days. A quiet supper out goes a long way with her.

# Mama June and Harlan

Mama June is 78 now, still in the home place up in Harlan. Stubborn as a mule about staying put, and I respect it.

Darl is right there and looks in on her, runs Whitaker Hauling out of the same town. I send what I can each month to help with her bills.

Need to get up the mountain more. The drive is nothing. Christmas we will all be up there. Her chicken and dumplings is still the best thing I ever ate.

# Worries

Writing these down so they quit rattling around at midnight.

- Margins are tighter than they were. Carriers want more, clients want less. Same old squeeze.
- The software decision feels bigger than it is. If I pick wrong I have sunk money and a learning curve on the whole team.
- Bringing Brand in is a blessing and a pressure. Do not want family and business to chew each other up.
- I am fifty with my own health to mind. Who runs this if I cannot? No real answer yet.

None of it is a fire today. Just the weight a man carries owning the thing. Put it down for the night.

# Software upgrade decision

Evaluating two systems to replace the old setup.

## FreightFlow Pro
- Cheaper monthly
- Team knows the look of it
- Support has been slow when we have called

## RoutePoint Logistics Suite
- More money but better carrier vetting tools
- Cleaner reporting for the auto parts clients
- Demo impressed Travis and Lorrie

Leaning RoutePoint. The vetting piece alone may pay for itself with the automotive work. Want Dale to run the numbers before I sign.

# Brand at the company

Brand started as junior associate in January. So far so good.

He is quick with the load board and good on the phone once he settles in. Gets ahead of himself on rates sometimes, wants to win the deal too fast.

My job is to let him make small mistakes where they do not cost much, and be there when one gets big. Bren is good with him too, keeps him organized.

He handled a rate con solo today and it was clean. That is the kind of thing I want to see.

# Brisket log

Keeping track so I quit relearning the same lessons.

## Last cook (early June)
- 13 lb packer, trimmed the hard fat
- Salt and coarse pepper, kept it simple
- Oak and a little hickory in the brick pit
- Held 250, wrapped in butcher paper at 165 internal
- Pulled at 203, rested two hours in the cooler

Best bark I have gotten yet. Donna said the point was too rich, so I will render the fat cap a touch longer next time. See [[Rub and sauce notes]].

# Rub and sauce notes

## House rub
- Coarse black pepper and kosher salt base
- Touch of paprika and garlic for the chicken and pork, leave it off the brisket

## Sauce
- Vinegar forward for pulled pork, the way they do it back home
- Tomato based and a little sweet for the ribs, that is what the kids like

Note to self: stop buying sauce. Mine is better and cheaper.

# Douglas Lake log

## Late May trip
- Out early before the boat traffic
- Crappie were biting in the brush off the points
- Kept a mess of them, fried up that evening
- Water still a little stained from the spring rain

Good morning on the water. Keith came along and we solved most of the world's problems between bites.

Big Douglas Lake trip is planned for November 7 through 9. Marking the calendar now so nothing crowds it out.

# Cherokee Lake and the Smokies

Cherokee is closer and good for a quick evening run after work. Bass mostly, nothing to write home about but it clears my head.

Still want to get back up in the Smokies for fly fishing this summer. The little streams up high run cold and clear. It is a different kind of patience than bait fishing the lake.

Need to re-spool the fly reel and check my waders before I go.

# Map collection

Keeping a running note on the historical maps I have and the ones I am hunting.

## Have
- Reprint of the Great Valley Railroad corridor, late 1800s
- Two old Cumberland Gap survey maps, framed in the office
- A TVA-era map of the Tennessee Valley lakes before they filled

## Want
- An original L&N rail map through Harlan County
- Anything showing the old wagon roads through the Gap

There is a dealer in Asheville who said he would call if a good Gap map came in. See [[Cumberland Gap railroad notes]].

# Cumberland Gap railroad notes

Reading on how the rail lines pushed through the Gap. Funny how it ties to my own line of work, just a hundred and some years back.

- The Gap was the bottleneck for moving freight and people west for generations
- Rail through that country was an engineering headache, all grade and tunnel
- My people in Harlan worked the coal that those same lines hauled out

There is a straight line from those rail cars to my brokerage. We are all just trying to move the load from where it is to where it needs to be.

# Garden log

## Early June
- Tomatoes are setting fruit, six plants
- Peppers slow but coming
- Squash already trying to take over the bed
- Put in a second row of beans

Mornings I water before the heat. It is a good way to start the day before the phone gets going. Donna wants more herbs by the patio, will dig that bed this weekend.
